modelBoundary: Optional overlay only. The normal twenty-load LM-7 catalog is unchanged.
No input watts or allocations are chosen to reproduce 25 A, 12 A or a reserve endpoint.
Cross-vehicle transfer error and missing-power error have no established numeric bound.
Values are nominal branch inputs; constant-power representation is an approximation.
Heater availability and demand are separate. Candidates require explicit duty assumptions.
LM-7 values take precedence where sources overlap; conflicting LM-8 comms/audio/EPS-display values are withheld.
Unmodeled inverter losses and transient solenoid loads are not backfilled as residual watts.
Single-feed AEA constraints prevent duplicate debit; dual-feed sharing remains unresolved.

GLYCOL selects primary pump 1 or 2; INST (SEC) selects instrumentation, not the secondary pump motor. SUIT FAN 1/2 selects its motor and OFF removes fan power. Automatic transfer after pump failure is not a normal selector state and is outside this overlay.
Each primary glycol pump is supplied from CDR DC through its own breaker and GLYCOL PUMP switch. AUTO TRNFR is a relay-control branch, not a pump load.

OFF removes AGS operating power but retains ASA heater supply. STANDBY applies full ASA power and AEA warmup. OPERATE applies full ASA and AEA power. AEA warmup watts and thermostat duty are not established.
LMP DC feeds AEA, ASA, ATCA power supply and AGS ATCA selection/bias branch. AEA has another CDR feed; ASA breaker also acts as its on/off supply.
CDR DC provides AEA main supply and ATCA PGNS selection/bias supply. The table does not establish redundant AEA feed sharing.
DECA PWR applies CDR DC to DECA for engine-on function and trim-fail circuit. ENG CONT supplies engine-related control functions; its operating draw is not proven constant by closing its breaker.
SUIT FAN DP supplies LMP DC to the suit fan differential-pressure sensor. Its electrical supply is not gated by the selected fan motor switch.

4CB50 supplies LMP DC to RCS TEMP/PRESS indicators and talkbacks. 4CB103 supplies LMP DC to main-propulsion temperature/pressure indicators and talkbacks. 4CB121 supplies LMP DC to the RCS propellant-quantity device. LM-8 Table 5-III assigns 4CB121 to CDR; that transfer is withheld.

FWD or OVHD energizes the corresponding COAS connector from CDR DC through the FLIGHT DISPLAYS COAS breaker. OFF removes connector power. Brightness dependence is not quantified by the LM-8 maximum/nominal branch entry.

Thirty-two heaters serve sixteen TCAs: two per TCA, one on each redundant bank. Each element is 17.5 W at 24 V. Four elements per quad/bank imply 70 W at 24 V. Primary thermostat setpoint is 140 +/- 8 F, redundant 147 +/- 7 F, with a 2 F deadband. Supply is described as 28 V DC.

Bank 1 provides automatic heater control without override. Bank 2 AUTO uses temperature control, OFF interrupts power, and MAN bypasses temperature control to hold 28 V on its heaters. Breaker closure is not thermostat demand.

excludedModes.reason: LM-8 input-power row assigns CDR while the LM-7 control table and modeled breaker assign LMP. Withheld pending cross-vehicle circuit adjudication; no silent bus transfer.
Both AEA feeds closed has no known sharing; standby/warmup watts unavailable.
The AC input mode gate and partial-supply response require circuit review; not a switch-only draw.
PGNS/AGS selector and mode bias paths do not establish a constant branch operating law.
Actual jet commands and dwell times required; closed TCA breaker is not firing.
Watts and amp columns disagree at28V; function/state consumption unresolved.
Momentary, solenoid or engine-state duty not established.
COAS local rheostat/connector occupancy and light brightness/duty unquantified; no full-bright current assumed.
Table describes CDR AND LMP aggregate; no invented per-bus split.
Power mode, standby and heater overlap unresolved; manual MCC kept LGC and IMU operate off.
Use printed watts only when included; never silently correct printed amp values.

uncertainty.numericalTableResolution: As printed:0.1W for most power rows; no calibration accuracy inferred.
uncertainty.interpretation: Decimal resolution is not an accuracy bound or historical acceptance tolerance.
